# OQ-25 Decision Package: Canonical Price Extremes

**Doc:** CBR-DEC-025 · **Version:** v1.1 · **Date:** 2026-09-15 · **Status:** **APPROVED by owner ruling D16 (2026-09-15)**; see §0.
The analysis below is the v1.0 package as submitted.
**Evidence:** `reports/oq25-extrema-evidence.{md,json}` (generated by `src/cbr/data/oq25_extrema_study.py`) plus Phase 9

## 0. Owner ruling D16 (2026-09-15)

| Id | Item | Ruling |
|---|---|---|
| D16-1 | Canonical source | **APPROVED.** STRUCTURE PRICE = tick-derived midpoint; EXECUTION PRICE = tick-derived bid/ask. Structure is authoritative for swing highs/lows, range highs/lows and boundaries, extension highs/lows, liquidity takes/sweeps, extreme-sensitive structure logic, stop anchor/reference levels and target construction. Execution is authoritative for entry fills, stop and target touches, spread, bid/ask execution and execution-cost simulation. **One OHLC series is never used for both** |
| D16-2 | Two-price-series rule | **APPROVED.** Access guards: structure/signal code can't silently consume bid/ask; execution code can't substitute mid for fills; every derived bar/source records whether it is STRUCTURE or EXECUTION. The distinction is visible in schemas, manifests and reports |
| D16-3 | V-1 TradingView/FOREXCOM validation | **APPROVED, not required before Phase 11.** It is a **hard requirement before Phase 13 parity is declared complete**. If the export reveals material structure differences, stop and reopen OQ-25 before parity can pass. Never choose the source that produces better trades |
| D16-4 | Full gold tick history | **DEFERRED.** No 2018-2026 download yet. First complete Phases 11-13 and the gate-required cross-feed/structure sensitivity checks, then decide the needed historical granularity. The acquisition strategy stays open (OQ-33): full tick history / targeted windows around armed candidates / another validated tick source / staged resumable hybrid, chosen on fidelity, reproducibility and execution needs, never profitability |
| D16-5 | Phase 11 | **APPROVED** on the currently downloaded tick days once this ruling is recorded and guard tests exist. No baseline profitability, no optimization, no holdout P&L |
| D16-6 | Candle files | Useful for open/close checks, download/integrity diagnostics, bid/ask cross-checks, coarse history and validation support. **Not canonical** for structure-sensitive highs/lows; averaged candle-file mid highs/lows are never canonical extremes |
| D16-7 | GC futures | Cross-feed reference, broad-history research source, volume source and possible later OQ-24 baseline-feed candidate. **Not approved** as the canonical structure feed (structure disagreement too large) |

## 1. The question

Which price series is authoritative for the historical highs and lows the CBR engine uses? They feed swing points,
range boundaries, extension extremes, liquidity takes and sweeps, extreme-sensitive structure shifts, stop placement,
target construction, parity with Tom, custom execution, Backtesting.py parity and the eventual TradingView version.

This document also answers the owner's design question: should the project keep **two price concepts**?

- **STRUCTURE PRICE:** swings, ranges, extensions, signal logic.
- **EXECUTION PRICE:** bid/ask fills, stop and target touches.

## 2. Evidence base

| Item | Scope |
|---|---|
| XAUUSD full days with ticks | **21 days, 28,571 minutes**: 16 AC-11A sample days (dev 2018-2022, validation 2023-2024) + 5 fixture days (Oct 21-24 and Nov 10 2025, holdout period, data-fidelity use only, logged) |
| DXY CFD tick windows | 7 windows (3-5 h each; Phase 9) |
| Series compared | `candle_mid` (Dukascopy candle file, SIDE_EXTREME_MEAN) · `candle_bid`, `candle_ask` · `tick_mid` · `tick_bid`, `tick_ask` · `gc` (Databento GC front month) |
| Structure parameters | Frozen V1 values only: swing k = 3.0 × ATR(1m,14) (LTF), stop buffer 0.1 ATR. Nothing varied |
| Mismatch tolerance | XAUUSD $0.05, DXY 0.005 (config/data_quality.yaml) |

### 2.1 Candle-file vs tick-derived extremes (XAUUSD, 28,571 minutes)

| Comparison | High mismatch | Low mismatch | Largest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `candle_mid` vs `tick_mid` | **1.99%** of minutes | **2.04%** | $2.43 high / $2.36 low (2020-06-17, spread spike) |
| `candle_bid` vs `tick_bid` | **1 minute** of 28,571 | 0 | $0.15 (2024-04-12 15:54: the candle file has a bid quote, 2391.065, that isn't in the tick file, whose max is 2390.915) |
| `candle_ask` vs `tick_ask` | same 1 minute | 0 | $0.13 |
| `tick_bid` vs `tick_mid` (half-spread offset) | 99.9% | 99.96% | median $0.11-0.39 by day; $5.02 (2020-06-17) |

**The artificial mid extreme depends on the market regime** (share of minutes > $0.05, high / low):

| Year | Minutes | High | Low | Days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2018 | 2,760 | 0.07% | 0.07% | 2 |
| 2019 | 2,744 | 0.03% | 0.07% | 2 |
| 2020 | 4,140 | **3.24%** | **2.87%** | 3 (incl. Mar 2020 volatility, Jun 17 spread spike) |
| 2021 | 2,760 | 0.22% | 0.10% | 2 |
| 2022 | 3,987 | 0.43% | 0.53% | 3 |
| 2023 | 2,760 | 0.03% | 0.10% | 2 |
| 2024 | 2,640 | 0.27% | 0.15% | 2 |
| 2025 (holdout fixtures) | 6,780 | **5.89%** | **6.34%** | 5 (2025-10-22: 14.3% / 13.5%) |

Per-day p99 of |candle_mid − tick_mid| ranges from $0.01 (2023) to $0.25 (2025-10-22). DXY windows: 0% mismatch on most,
but **36.8% / 42.1%** on the 2018-01-17 window (max 0.3185) and 6.7% / 6.1% on 2020-03-16.

Why it matters beyond the size: the distortion **isn't stationary**. It is concentrated in volatile or wide-spread regimes
and in the 2025 holdout period. A structure series built on it would carry a data artifact that differs between the
development, validation and holdout splits.

### 2.3 Stop-level touches (3,732 hypothetical levels, no trades)

A level is placed beyond every closed 15m candle's high (+0.1 ATR) and low (−0.1 ATR). The test is whether it's touched
within 30 minutes. Stops above are touched by highs (a short's stop), stops below by lows (a long's stop).

| What differs | Touch disagreements |
|---|---|
| Artificial extremes only: candle_mid vs tick_mid for both structure and touches | **15 (0.40%)** |
| Execution side only: same tick_mid structure, touches on bid/ask vs on mid | **254 (6.8%)** |
| One stream vs two concepts: candle_mid for everything vs tick_mid structure + bid/ask touches | **257 (6.9%)** |
| Execution source: tick bid/ask vs candle-file bid/ask (same structure) | **0** |

**Reading:** the execution *side* matters about 17× more than artificial extremes. One OHLC stream for both structure
and execution gets roughly 7% of stop touches wrong. Candle-file bid/ask bars are an exact substitute for tick bid/ask at
1m.

### 2.4 Robustness of tick-derived mid

Only **3 of 57,142** tick_mid minute extremes (0.005%) were set by a quote whose spread exceeded 5× that hour's median.
Spread spikes barely move the synchronous mid.

### 2.5 Fidelity to Tom's chart (weak, n = 3)

| Tom's chart price | tick mid | tick bid | tick ask |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stop "at extension low" 4332.96 (2025-10-21 01:38) | **−0.005** | −0.365 | +0.355 |
| Live label close 4046.10 (2025-11-10 01:53) | −1.76 | −2.15 | −1.37 (a FOREX.com vs Dukascopy feed offset; not side-diagnostic) |
| Entry 4340.13 (2025-10-21 01:39, intrabar) | inside the minute's range on every side (not diagnostic) | | |

One informative point favours mid. It is **not** enough to establish whether Tom's FOREXCOM:XAUUSD chart is mid- or
bid-based. That needs validation test V-1 (§7).

## 3. Options evaluated

| Id | Option |
|---|---|
| **A** | Dukascopy candle-file OHLC (mid = mean of per-side extremes) |
| **B** | Tick-derived midpoint OHLC |
| **C** | Tick-derived bid OHLC |
| **D** | Tick-derived ask OHLC |
| **E** | Dual bid/ask bars with a derived reference mid series |
| **F** | Databento GC futures OHLC |
| **G** | Hybrid: spot for canonical structure, futures only for diagnostics / broad history |
| **H** (additional) | Cost-reduced hybrid: candle-file 1m mid for structure, candle-file bid/ask for 1m execution, ticks only around armed 5s entry windows |
| **I** (additional) | TradingView FOREXCOM:XAUUSD export (Tom's actual chart feed) |
| **J** (additional) | Candle-file open/close-only ("body") structure: synchronous, no wicks |

**E has two variants.** E-candle: bid/ask from candle files, mid = their average, which is option A's mid again. E-tick:
bid/ask from ticks, mid from the same synchronous ticks, which is B + C + D from one source. §5 recommends E-tick. The
evidence shows E-candle's execution half (candle bid/ask) is exact.

---

## 4. Two price concepts: STRUCTURE vs EXECUTION

The evidence supports keeping them separate:

1. **Different jobs, different truths.** Structure asks where the market's price went (a symmetric reference, the same
   for longs and shorts). Execution asks what a trader could trade (ask to buy, bid to sell).
2. **One stream is materially wrong for one of the jobs.** A mid stream gets about 7% of stop touches wrong (§2.3, side
   effect 6.8%). A bid (or ask) stream biases structure by the half-spread and turns spread spikes into false
   sweeps: 171 of 713 swept swings differ, 2.6% of 15m takes, 1.0% of 15m extension directions.
3. **The existing spec already implies it.** Primitives §8 anchors the stop at `oe_extreme` (structure) and fills "+
   slippage" with "+ spread" (execution). D14-1 keeps the contract on canonical stop *inputs*, resolved by the simulator
   at fill.
4. **A single tick source gives both, synchronously and reproducibly.** One download, one hash, three derived bar sets.

**Rule, if approved:** structure logic may only read `hl_method = TICK_MID` bars. Fills, stop and target touches may
only read side bars (`BID` / `ASK`). Enforced by tests (V-5).

---

## RECOMMENDED CANONICAL EXTREMA SOURCE

**Option E-tick (B + C + D from one tick source), used as two concepts:**

- **STRUCTURE PRICE = tick-derived midpoint OHLC (B, `TICK_MID`)** at 5s, 1m, 5m, 15m and 1h, rolled up deterministically
  from the same ticks. This is canonical for swings, range highs/lows and boundaries, extension extremes, takes/sweeps,
  extreme-sensitive shifts, and the stop anchor and target construction.
- **EXECUTION PRICE = tick-derived bid and ask OHLC (C + D)** at 5s: entries (buy at ask, sell at bid), stop and target
  touches (long exits observed on bid, short exits on ask). Candle-file bid/ask 1m bars are an **exact** cross-check
  (0 of 3,732 touch disagreements; 1 vendor-inconsistent minute in 28,571).
- **Candle-file OHLC (A)** is kept for open/close-only uses (Phase 10 DXY context, integrity checks) and never for
  structure extremes.

**Condition:** provisional on validation test **V-1**. A FOREXCOM:XAUUSD export must not show Tom's chart to be
materially closer to bid than to mid in highs/lows and timing. If V-1 contradicts mid, a structure-side revision (C) comes
back for owner decision; it isn't switched silently.

## SECOND-BEST OPTION

**H: cost-reduced hybrid.** Candle-file 1m mid for structure, candle-file bid/ask for 1m execution, ticks only around
armed 5s entry windows. It's viable only if a pre-declared study on a stratified tick sample shows the structure artifact
doesn't change **signal membership** (G2d wording). Costs:
- the artifact stays inside canonical structure and is regime-dependent (6% of 2025 minutes);
- which tick windows exist depends on engine output, coupling data to engine versions;
- structure runs at 1m while CBR15 shifts need 5s.

## REJECTED OPTIONS

- **A (candle-file OHLC for extremes):** non-synchronous mid, regime-dependent artificial extremes (2.0% overall, ~6% in
  2025), no 5s.
- **C or D alone (single side for everything):** half-spread bias; spread-spike false sweeps and takes; long/short
  asymmetry; still needs the other side for execution.
- **F (GC futures):** different market from Tom's spot; 84% swing agreement; 22-24% extension-timing disagreement;
  rolls and basis; 1m only.
- **G as a canonical history source:** futures must not fill canonical structure where spot exists. **Retained** in its
  diagnostic role only: cross-feed checks and G2b, as already governed.
- **I (TradingView export) as the source:** not reproducible, limited history, licensing. **Retained** as the fidelity
  reference for V-1.
- **J (body-only):** discards wick extremes that Tom's structure and stops use.

## WHY

1. It is the only option that is synchronous, free of artificial extremes (0.005% spread-set) **and** supports the spec's
   5-second logic for both models.
2. It avoids a data artifact that is non-stationary across the dev/validation/holdout splits.
3. Separating structure from execution removes about 7% stop-touch error without inventing any rule, and matches the
   machine spec's existing stop anchor + spread semantics (D14-1).
4. One raw source gives structure, execution and cross-checks with a single provenance hash.
5. The best available fidelity point (Tom's stop) matched mid within $0.005, subject to V-1.
6. The cost is time and disk, not money: 6-7 GB and a resumable download.

The selection used no profitability, trade outcomes or signal statistics.

## REQUIRED IMPLEMENTATION CHANGES (after approval only)

1. `src/cbr/data/bidask_bars.py`: tick → bid OHLC and ask OHLC bars (5s, 1m) with `hl_method = BID` / `ASK`, spread
   stats, tick counts.
2. `src/cbr/data/resampling.py`: causal roll-ups 5s → 1m → 5m → 15m → 1h from the same ticks. Each bar is usable only at
   its close; it must equal a direct tick resample (V-2).
3. Tick history layout and manifest: `data/raw/dukascopy/xauusd/ticks/YYYY-MM-DD.parquet` with hashes; resumable,
   serial, polite downloader with coverage and gap report. **The bulk download itself needs separate owner go-ahead.**
4. XAU vendor-gap detector analogous to D12 (spot ticks absent while GC trades), with MISSING handling.
5. Engine data-access guard: structure functions accept only `TICK_MID`; execution only `BID`/`ASK` (V-5).
6. Signal contract: `extremes_source = TICK_MID` required; `stop_rule.extension_extreme_source = TICK_MID`.
7. Config: `config/data_sources.yaml` recording the structure/execution sources, labelled IMPL with this decision id.
8. Keep candle files for open/close uses and for the side-bar cross-check (V-3).

| Id | Test | Pass condition (declared before running) |

| V-1 | **Tom-feed fidelity**: owner-provided FOREXCOM:XAUUSD 1m export for the course-example days; compare highs/lows and extreme timing against tick mid, bid and ask after removing the median level offset | Mid is not materially worse than bid/ask on swing-extreme timing and wick levels; otherwise a structure-side decision goes back to the owner |
| V-2 | Roll-up exactness: 5s → 1m → 5m → 15m → 1h equals a direct tick resample | 100% identical |
| V-3 | Candle-file bid/ask vs tick bid/ask on every downloaded day | Mismatches listed; each classified as DATA_ERROR (vendor) or PIPELINE_ERROR |
| V-4 | Candle-file open/close vs tick mid open/close (continuation of Phase 9 AC-03) | 100% identical |
| V-5 | Access guard: structure code refuses `SIDE_EXTREME_MEAN`/`BID`/`ASK`; execution refuses `TICK_MID` | Tests fail on violation |
| V-6 | Determinism: bars and manifests hash-identical on rebuild | 100% |
| V-7 | XAU tick-gap detection on full history (spot ticks absent while GC trades) | Every flagged interval classified; handled as MISSING |
| V-8 | Spread-spike influence on tick-mid extremes, full history | Reported per year (sample: 0.005%) |
| V-9 | Parity re-run: Tom's chart points and course examples on TICK_MID structure + side execution | Every difference classified (Phase 13) |
| V-10 | Coverage report per trading day: tick hours present vs expected session | Gaps listed; none silently dropped |

## HISTORICAL DATA IMPLICATIONS

- **XAUUSD full tick history 2018-01-01 → 2026-08-31 becomes required** before baselines (Phase 15). That's 65,112
  hourly requests, ≈ 6-7 GB, and 1.5-24 days of unattended serial downloading depending on vendor reliability. It
  **supersedes AC-11B's candle-file scope** for XAU. Owner go-ahead is needed before starting.
- The holdout period (2025-01 → 2026-08) ticks are downloaded but locked by the existing holdout controls.
- **DXY needs no ticks** (candle open/close context only).
- GC stays as-is (owned, diagnostic).
- Interacts with **OQ-24**: this recommendation makes spot the natural canonical structure feed. Futures can remain a
  diagnostic, or a G2b-gated alternative only if the owner chooses.

## PHASE 11 IMPACT

- The CBR15/CBR1H engines are built on `TICK_MID` structure bars and emit stop inputs anchored on `TICK_MID` extremes. No
  provisional highs/lows.
- **Phase 11 can start on the already-downloaded 21 full tick days plus fixture windows**, before full history exists.
  Engine development and unit/parity tests don't need full history.
- The implementation changes (bid/ask builder, roll-ups, access guard) are the first Phase 11 tasks after approval.

## PHASE 14 IMPACT

- 14A simulator: fills and touches on tick bid/ask 5s bars. Stop anchor from `TICK_MID` plus fill-time spread per
  D14-1/OQ-28.
- 14B Backtesting.py: approximation B (side series per direction, CBR-ARCH-014 §6.1) maps directly onto `BID`/`ASK` bars.
  Structure columns come precomputed from `TICK_MID`.
- Candle-file bid/ask 1m provides an exact independent cross-check of execution bars.

## TRADINGVIEW IMPACT

- Pine sees only TradingView's own FOREXCOM OHLC, whose side (bid or mid) is unverified. Pine structure therefore can't
  replicate `TICK_MID` exactly.
- Expected parity noise is at least the §2.2 bid-vs-mid rates (≈ 4% swing mismatch, ≈ 2.6% of 15m takes) if the TV feed is
  bid-based. That's to be measured in Phase 26 and declared, like `SIMPLIFIED-ENTRY`.
- V-1 also serves as the first TradingView-fidelity measurement.

## OPEN RISKS

1. **Tom's chart side is unverified** (n = 1 informative point). V-1 needs an owner-provided export.
2. **Download reliability:** today ≈ 32 s/file with retries; full history could take weeks.
3. **Vendor inconsistency:** 1 minute in 28,571 where the candle file holds a quote that isn't in the tick file. Tick
   files are treated as the raw truth, and such cases are logged (V-3).
4. **Evidence coverage:** 21 days (5 in 2025). The regime dependence suggests more variation exists; full-history V-8
   and V-3 will measure it.
5. **Two-concept discipline:** mixing structure and execution bars in code would silently reintroduce errors. Access
   guards (V-5) are mandatory.
6. **Storage growth:** 6-7 GB locally (gitignored). Backups are the owner's choice.
7. **TradingView divergence** is a structural, declared limitation of the downstream indicator, not of the research
   engine.
